rationale: The plan correctly identifies that a 1-vs-1 design supports no dispersion estimate and therefore no inferential test, and it consistently enforces this: size factors only, no DESeq() GLM or Wald test, descriptive log2FC with the numerator/denominator stated, and an explicit acceptance check that no p-value or significance label appears in the DE output. QC is design-aware (library sizes, distributions, vst, pairwise distance, with a correct note that PCA is degenerate at n=2), the >=10 counts in >=1 sample filter is minimal and justified, and normalization stays inside the median-of-ratios framework with no pre-scaling. The report is exemplary: it leads with the limitation, names the replicated design (>=3 per group) needed for inference, and carries versions, thresholds, and a reproducibility record. The main weakness is the enrichment step: although the collection, version, size window, universe, and ranking metric are all explicit and the results are hedged, running fgsea on a fold change vector derived from a single pair of samples reintroduces set-level p-values into an analysis that the plan itself argues can produce none, and enrichment is not warranted here at all.
